weekly: INTRODUCTION: This course is designed somewhat differently from most cultural studies courses. Focusing more on works in Critical Philosophy and Social Theory, it is more like an “underview” rather than an overview of Cultural Studies. And, seen from below, it would not be an exaggeration to say that what came to be called cultural studies in recent years essentially consists of critical analyses of cultural practices and representations. The ultimate aim of the course, therefore, can be summarized as understanding how these critical analyses are carried out.
The Origins of Modern Social Theory and Cultural Studies - The Enlightenment, “Representation,” and Kant's Critical Method.
The Concept of Ideology and its Vicissitudes.
Nietzsche and genealogy of modern values and institutions.
Moving beyond Structuralism? Bourdieu on Habitus, Capital, Social Space, Reflexivity and the Logic of Practice.
New Problematizations of Modernity in the Twentieth Century: Adorno on Enlightenment, Rationalization and Culture Industry.
Foucault on Discourse, Power and Knowledge.
Technologies and Practices of the Self

Workshop: Presentations by seminar participants. The choice of topics and texts is necessarily limited by time and energy considerations. To alleviate this limitation, in the final part of the course, the participants will have a chance to present and discuss topics that are not covered in the course outline, focusing on works published in the last few years in the field of Cultural Studies.

outcomes: Develop field-related conceptual knowledge in Social and Behavioral Sciences and of relationships between concepts; ability to consider the reflections conceptual knowledge in practice (K1 and K2)
Have basic knowledge on causes and consequences of transformations of societies (K4)
Have knowledge on social research and planning and command of its practices (K5)
Have command of statistical knowledge and logical reasoning processes required by Social and Behavioral Sciences (K6)

Have the skill of improving and deepening the updated and advanced knowledge from the field and sub-fields, and of providing original definitions that can innovate the field through original thinking and/or research at expert level (K7)
Analyze theoretical knowledge and evaluate its reflections in practice (S1)
Have command of basic concepts in the field and have the knowledge of producing works compatible with academic rules by using these concepts (S2)
Evaluate the knowledge acquired in the field with a critical approach by investigating causal relationships (L1)
Identify deficiencies in knowledge and in practice related to the field (L2)
Show capacity to keep interest and motivation in the field continuous and alive (L3)
Develop new ideas in the field through using advanced level of intellectual processes such as creative and critical thinking, problem solving and decision-making (L5)
Communicate the field-related knowledge and skills in writing and speaking (C1)
Share field-related solutions supported by scientific data with competent peers (C2)
Defend original views during the discussions with experts about the subjects in the field and establish effective communication to show competence in the field (C5)
Monitor the developments in the field and communicate with peers by using a foreign language at least at a level of European Language Portfolio C1 (C6)

Have sufficient awareness about the issues of universality of social rights, social justice, quality and cultural values, together with environmental protection and occupational health and safety (F3)
Have an open attitudes towards change and innovation (F4)
